about.githubDescription: Zotero Metadata Assistant: a CUNY AI Lab plugin for Zotero 7 and later that proposes missing book and article metadata from Open Library, Google Books and Crossref for your review, and imports pasted bibliographies with optional AI parsing.

responses.text:
Thanks for the card. It was accurate for 1.0.0, and we've addressed each finding in 1.1.1, released October 27, 2026.

Capabilities: the two medium findings, the zotero://plugin and zotero://ztoolkit-debug handlers, came from zotero-plugin-toolkit, which registers them on its own. The plugin never used either. Toolkit 6.0.0 still includes them, so from 1.1.0 our build swaps the toolkit's two bridge modules for inert stand-ins. Neither handler is in the released file, and the build fails if either string reappears.

Updates: 1.0.0 was uploaded by hand and the release/update.json the manifest points to was never published. 1.1.1 is built and published by our GitHub Actions release workflow, and the update address now serves 1.1.1.

Source transparency: the 1.1.1 XPI has a GitHub build-provenance attestation tying it to tag v1.1.1 at commit 6ee7e68, so you can check that the release file was built from the public source with `gh attestation verify zotero-metadata-assistant.xpi --repo CUNY-AI-Lab/zotero-autofill`.

Compatibility: 1.1.1 supports Zotero 7 through 10.0.x. Zotero 10's multi-selection broke bibliography import when several collections were selected, and that's fixed. Our integration tests pass against Zotero 10.0.6.

We'd be grateful if you'd grade 1.1.1, including the live Zotero 10 test.
responses.reply:
Thanks for the detailed write-up. The card now describes 1.1.1: neither zotero:// handler is in the release file, the update address serves 1.1.1, and it works with Zotero 7 through 10.

We also ran 1.1.1 in Zotero 10 (10.0.3) in our sandbox. It loaded, we opened its settings and clicked its three menu items, and everything it did is on its card; it contacted only api.crossref.org and api.semanticscholar.org. With that live test, the grade is A+.

On the toolkit: 6.0.0 removes zotero://plugin and registers zotero://ztoolkit-debug only if a plugin calls DebugBridge.register() itself, so on 6.x the esbuild stand-ins shouldn't be needed. The check:bundle guard is worth keeping either way.

Our source check doesn't read GitHub build attestations yet. Yours is stronger evidence than what we check today, so attestation checks are on our list.

responses.text:
Thanks for re-checking at 1.2.0. The card says the plugin contacts a server you couldn't identify, `tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu`. That finding is correct, and here is what the server is.

`tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu` is the CUNY AI Lab Gateway, run by the CUNY AI Lab at the CUNY Graduate Center, the same lab that publishes this plugin. It is one of the plugin's three AI providers, next to OpenRouter and a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and it is the provider selected by default. The plugin contacts it in two cases:

- **The model list.** When the plugin's settings pane opens with the Gateway selected, and before an AI request, the plugin sends `GET https://tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu/v1/catalog` to fill the model menu. This request carries no key and no library data. It is refreshed at most once a day. Since 1.2.0 the menu is read live instead of being built in, which is why the host first appeared in your sandbox run.
- **AI requests.** Only after the user enters a Gateway key and runs an AI feature (parsing pasted bibliography text, or assessing possible matches), the plugin sends that text to `https://tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu/v1/chat/completions`. Without a key, no AI request is sent and catalogue lookup still works.

With OpenRouter selected, the same two cases go to `openrouter.ai`, and the Gateway is not contacted. With a custom endpoint, they go to the address the user enters.

1.3.0, released November 16, 2026, changes the catalogue side:

- Every catalogue request (Open Library, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Google Books) now sends a User-Agent naming the plugin and its version, as Open Library asks API clients to. AI-provider requests are unchanged.
- An ISBN lookup may make one extra Open Library request, for the work's description when the edition has none. A title and author search now fetches an Open Library edition record only for the match it chose, where it used to fetch every edition in the results.
- The review window can offer to fill Library Catalog and add an `Open Library ID` line to Extra. Nothing is saved until the user accepts it.

The hosts are otherwise the same as before: `openlibrary.org`, `api.crossref.org`, `api.semanticscholar.org` and `www.googleapis.com`.

Compatibility: the manifest declares Zotero 7 through 11.0.x. Our integration tests pass on the current Zotero release and beta.

We'd be grateful if you'd grade 1.3.0 with the Gateway identified.
responses.reply:
Thanks for identifying the server. We checked 1.3.0, the release on the card now, and the code matches your description. The Gateway is the default provider (`aiProvider` is `"cail"` in prefs.js). The model list is a plain GET to tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu/v1/catalog with no key and no library data, refreshed at most once a day (zotero-metadata-assistant.js:941 and 974). AI requests to /v1/chat/completions (line 1325) are sent only once a Gateway key is set. One detail for readers: besides pasted bibliography text, the AI features send an item's title, author and year, and when assessing matches, the candidate records' title, author, year, publisher and ISBN (lines 1431 to 1481).

The card now lists tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu as a developer's server, in place of "a server we couldn't identify." Our rules give the developer's own servers the same level as an unidentified one, medium. We can say where data goes, not what happens to it once it arrives. So data sharing stays medium, and the grade stays B. That isn't a judgment of the Gateway. A user who prefers a provider the card lists as a named AI service can choose OpenRouter or their own endpoint in the plugin's settings. With OpenRouter selected, the code doesn't contact the Gateway at all, though the card grades the default setup.

The 1.3.0 catalogue changes are on the card as you describe them: the same four catalogue hosts (openlibrary.org, api.crossref.org, api.semanticscholar.org, www.googleapis.com), and it works with Zotero 10 and the Zotero 11 beta.

responses.text:
1.3.1, released November 19, 2026, adds one host to the catalogue side: `api.datacite.org`, the public REST API of [DataCite](https://datacite.org/), the DOI registration agency for arXiv, Zenodo and most other repositories. We are writing before you re-check so the new address is identified.

Why it was added: until 1.3.0 an item's DOI was looked up at Crossref only. arXiv and Zenodo DOIs are registered with DataCite, so Crossref answered 404 and preprints came back as not found (issue #35).

The plugin contacts DataCite in two cases, both during a metadata lookup (the menu command, or the automatic lookup on new items if the user has enabled it):

- **A DOI Crossref does not hold.** For an item that is not a book and already has a DOI, the plugin asks Crossref first, as before. Only if Crossref answers 404 does it send `GET https://api.datacite.org/dois/<DOI>`.
- **A preprint with an arXiv ID and no DOI.** If the item's Archive ID, Extra or URL carries an arXiv ID, the plugin sends the same request for that paper's arXiv DOI (`10.48550/arXiv.<id>`).

The request carries the DOI and the User-Agent naming the plugin and its version. It carries no key, no title or author, and no other library data. As with every catalogue, what comes back is shown in the review window and nothing is saved until the user accepts it.

Nothing else about where data goes has changed. The other hosts are the same as in 1.3.0: `openlibrary.org`, `api.crossref.org`, `api.semanticscholar.org`, `www.googleapis.com`, and the AI provider the user selects (`tools.ailab.gc.cuny.edu` by default, or `openrouter.ai`, or a custom endpoint).

Compatibility is unchanged: the manifest declares Zotero 7 through 11.0.x.
